response_json.request: Add bigger amount of cylindrical holes into the red platforms to decrease their weights. Amount of patterns can be chosen by editor.

actions.operation: Add a pattern or patterns of cylindrical holes

parameters.amount: a bigger amount than currently present

actions.relational_constraint: The cylindrical holes are to extend into the red platforms.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the red platform geometry, determine the existing hole or pattern amount used as the basis for 'bigger amount,' and select the pattern amount and arrangement.
steps: Localize the two platform solids independently from the linkage and pins: R01/F001 is the lower red platform body in SOLID 4, and R02/F004 is the upper platform body in SOLID 5. Do not apply the subtraction to R03 linkage solids or R04 pin solids.

Use the large X-Z platform surfaces as sketch supports. For the lower platform, use FACE 64 at y=7.752975 mm, with FACE 67 at y=-4.247025 mm as the opposing through-cut exit face. For the upper platform, use FACE 103 at y=50.605773 mm, with FACE 106 at y=38.605773 mm as the opposing exit face.
Create a weight-reduction hole sketch on FACE 64 of F001. Draw equal-diameter circles and constrain their centers with a rectangular or staggered two-dimensional pattern in the available X-Z area.

Exclude keep-out zones around the lower elongated guide slot F002, including FACE 72, FACE 73, FACE 78, and FACE 80, and around the fixed pivot bore F003/FACE 79. Maintain sufficient material around the platform perimeter and between neighboring holes so that the support and bending-resistance functions of F001 are retained.

As an editor-selected initial pattern, use eight holes per platform in two Z rows and four X columns. A suitable starting layout is a 5 mm hole diameter, X centers near -10, 2, 14, and 26 mm, and Z centers near -10 and 10 mm. The editor may increase or decrease the row and column counts after enforcing edge, slot, pivot, and minimum-web constraints, but the final quantity should represent multiple new holes rather than replacing the existing functional bore.

Cut the lower-platform circles through all of SOLID 4 in the negative-Y direction, traversing the full 12 mm platform thickness from FACE 64 to FACE 67. Use a through-all or up-to-next termination so every resulting cavity has a cylindrical wall and no residual floor.
Create the corresponding sketch on FACE 103 of F004. Reuse the same diameter, spacing, and center coordinates to produce a balanced matching pattern on the upper platform.

Exclude keep-out zones around upper guide slot F005, including FACE 111, FACE 112, FACE 117, and FACE 119, and around fixed pivot bore F006/FACE 118. Ensure that no new hole intersects the guide slot, fixed pivot interface, platform edges, or the linkage operating envelope.

Cut the upper-platform circles through all of SOLID 5 in the negative-Y direction from FACE 103 to FACE 106. Perform this cut only on the upper platform solid so the nearby crossed links and pins remain unchanged.

If manufacturing requirements permit, apply a small equal deburring chamfer of approximately 0.3 to 0.5 mm to the two circular mouths of each new hole. Do not propagate the chamfer to the guide-slot or pivot-bore edges.

Regenerate the assembly and check that all new holes are open through the platform thickness, that F002/F005 still permit pin translation, and that F003/F006 retain uninterrupted cylindrical bearing surfaces.

Compare platform mass before and after the cuts and verify minimum ligament widths and platform bending strength under the intended load. Reduce hole diameter or pattern count if structural verification shows excessive stress or deflection.

intention: Decrease the weights of the red platforms.
